library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2019_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2019_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-47876-0>

Kim et al. (2019) refitted the integrated tacrolimus (TAC) and mycophenolate
mofetil (MMF) model of their earlier healthy-volunteer study (packaged as
`Kim_2018_tacrolimus`) to steady-state data from stable kidney transplant
recipients. The structure is unchanged: TAC is a two-compartment model with a
lag time, MMF is described by mycophenolic acid (MPA) and its two glucuronides
MPAG and AcMPAG with enterohepatic recirculation of MPAG, and MPA plasma
concentration lowers TAC apparent clearance through an inverse-exponential
term (Eq. 1). The transplant refit adds two genotype effects on the MMF
metabolites and re-estimates the disposition parameters; the absorption, lag,
and enterohepatic-circulation parameters were fixed to the healthy-volunteer
values. This is the paper's final model (Table 2, "Final model" columns).

# Population

Thirty-two Korean kidney transplant recipients at a median 5.7 years
(0.6-10.4) after transplantation took part (Table 1). Median age was 52 years
(20-70), median weight 62.7 kg (43.9-102.4), and 20 (63%) were male. Graft
function was near normal (MDRD eGFR 35.0-85.7 mL/min/1.73 m2). Patients took
TAC (Prograf, median 2 mg/day, range 1-6) and MMF (CellCept, median
1,000 mg/day, range 500-2,000) twice daily with prednisolone, on a dose that had
been stable for at least two weeks. Blood was sampled before the morning dose
and 1, 2, 3 and 4 h after it. Thirteen patients (40.6%) were CYP3A5 expressers
(*1/*1 or *1/*3), and 15 (46.9%) each were T carriers of SLCO1B3 rs4149117 and
UGT2B7 rs7439366.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kim_2019_tacrolimus")$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its Table 2 row in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Kim_2019_tacrolimus.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F TAC) | 21.9 L/h | Table 2 CL TAC; Eq. 1 |
| `lvc` (V/F TAC) | 103 L | Table 2 V TAC |
| `lka` (Ka TAC, fixed) | 1.78 1/h | Table 2 Ka TAC (FIX) |
| `lk23`, `lk32` | 0.803, 0.583 1/h | Table 2 k23, k32 |
| `ltlag` (fixed) | 0.59 h | Table 2 Lag time (FIX) |
| `e_cyp3a5_cl` | 1.49 | Table 2 CYP3A5 on CL TAC; Eq. 1 |
| `e_cmpa_cl` | 0.06 mL/ug | Table 2 Interaction; Eq. 1 |
| `lcl_mpa` (CL/F MPA) | 3.27 L/h | Table 2 CL MPA |
| `lvc_mpa` (V/F MPA) | 23.2 L | Table 2 V MPA |
| `lka_mpa` (fixed) | 2.29 1/h | Table 2 Ka MPA (FIX) |
| `lk56`, `lk65` | 1.75, 0.0089 1/h | Table 2 k56, k65 |
| `f_mpag` (fixed) | 0.85 | Table 2 f MPA (FIX) |
| `e_ugt2b7_k59` | 0.812 | Table 2 UGT2B7 on k59 |
| `lvc_mpag` | 1.76 L | Table 2 V MPAG |
| `e_slco1b3_vc_mpag` | 1.2 | Table 2 SLCO1B3 on V MPAG |
| `lk70` | 0.103 1/h | Table 2 k70 |
| `lehc`, `lk84`, `lmtime1`, `lmtime2` (fixed) | 0.367, 18.4 1/h, 7.96 h, 1 h | Table 2 EHC, k84, MTIME1, MTIME2 (FIX) |
| `lvc_acmpag`, `lk90` (fixed) | 13.9 L, 0.407 1/h | Table 2 V AcMPAG, k90 (FIX) |

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The paper's simulation crossed TAC dose (1 or 2 mg bid), MMF dose (500 or
1,000 mg bid), CYP3A5, SLCO1B3 and UGT2B7 genotype (32 populations of 1,000).
Here four arms cross MMF dose with CYP3A5 status, 200 subjects each, and
TAC dose, SLCO1B3 and UGT2B7 status are drawn 50:50 within each arm. A fifth
arm mirrors the study cohort for the Figure 1 comparison: 1 mg TAC bid and
500 mg MMF bid (the median doses) with genotypes at the Table 1 frequencies.

Every subject receives 14 days of twice-daily dosing and is sampled over the
last 12-h interval (doses at 0, 12, ..., 324 h; trough at 336 h). The reason
for 14 days rather than a true steady state is set out in the next section.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190813)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190813)

n_per_arm <- 200L
n_days <- 14L
last_dose <- 24 * n_days - 12
obs_times <- c(last_dose - 0.01, last_dose + seq(0.25, 12, by = 0.25))

make_arm <- function(n, arm, mmf_mg, cyp, p_slco, p_ugt, tac_choices, id_offset) {
  tac_mg <- sample(tac_choices, n, replace = TRUE)
  cyp_i <- if (is.na(cyp)) stats::rbinom(n, 1L, 13 / 32) else rep(cyp, n)
  slco <- stats::rbinom(n, 1L, p_slco)
  ugt <- stats::rbinom(n, 1L, p_ugt)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = tac_mg[i], cmt = "depot", ii = 12, addl = 2 * n_days - 1) |>
      rxode2::et(amt = mmf_mg, cmt = "depot_mpa", ii = 12, addl = 2 * n_days - 1) |>
      rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central")
    df <- as.data.frame(ev)
    df$id <- id_offset + i
    df$arm <- arm
    df$tac_daily <- 2 * tac_mg[i]
    df$CYP3A5_EXPR <- cyp_i[i]
    df$SNP_SLCO1B3_RS4149117_T_CARRIER <- slco[i]
    df$SNP_UGT2B7_RS7439366_T_CARRIER <- ugt[i]
    df
  }))
}

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                                ~mmf_mg, ~cyp,
  "CYP3A5 expresser, MMF 500 mg bid",       500,    1L,
  "CYP3A5 expresser, MMF 1,000 mg bid",    1000,    1L,
  "CYP3A5 non-expresser, MMF 500 mg bid",   500,    0L,
  "CYP3A5 non-expresser, MMF 1,000 mg bid", 1000,   0L
)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(k) {
    make_arm(n_per_arm, arms$arm[k], arms$mmf_mg[k], arms$cyp[k],
             p_slco = 0.5, p_ugt = 0.5, tac_choices = c(1, 2),
             id_offset = (k - 1L) * n_per_arm)
  }),
  make_arm(n_per_arm, "Study cohort", 500, NA, p_slco = 15 / 32,
           p_ugt = 15 / 32, tac_choices = 1, id_offset = 4L * n_per_arm)
)
# Two endpoints are declared, so observation rows carry dvid = 1 and every
# endpoint is returned as a column.
events$dvid <- ifelse(events$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "cmt")]))
```

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2019_tacrolimus")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events,
  keep = c("arm", "tac_daily", "CYP3A5_EXPR"),
  returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  maxsteps = 1e6
)
sim <- dplyr::mutate(sim, tad = time - last_dose)
stopifnot(
  length(unique(sim$id)) == 5L * n_per_arm,
  all(is.finite(sim$Cc)), all(is.finite(sim$Cc_mpa)),
  # 9 ODE states in Figure 2 order; an observable injected as a compartment
  # would add a state and shift the slots.
  identical(rxode2::rxode2(mod)$state,
            c("depot", "central", "peripheral1", "depot_mpa", "central_mpa",
              "peripheral1_mpa", "central_mpag", "gallbladder", "central_acmpag"))
)
```

# How long a dosing history?

The MPA peripheral return constant is small (k65 = 0.0089 1/h), so the MPA
peripheral compartment fills over months. A typical patient's MPA trough on
500 mg bid, and through Eq. 1 the TAC trough, keeps rising long after two
weeks:

```{r history}
typical_trough <- function(days, mmf_mg, cyp) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "depot", ii = 12, addl = 2 * days - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = mmf_mg, cmt = "depot_mpa", ii = 12, addl = 2 * days - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(24 * days, cmt = "central")
  d <- as.data.frame(ev)
  d$dvid <- ifelse(d$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  d$CYP3A5_EXPR <- cyp
  d$SNP_SLCO1B3_RS4149117_T_CARRIER <- 0
  d$SNP_UGT2B7_RS7439366_T_CARRIER <- 0
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, d, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
                       useLinCmt = FALSE, maxsteps = 1e6)
  s[nrow(s), c("Cc", "Cc_mpa", "Cc_mpag", "Cc_acmpag")]
}

hist_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(7, 14, 21, 28, 56), function(days) {
  r <- typical_trough(days, 500, 0)
  data.frame(days = days, tac_cd = r$Cc / 2, mpa = r$Cc_mpa,
             mpag = r$Cc_mpag, acmpag = r$Cc_acmpag)
}))
hist_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-days, \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Days of bid dosing" = days,
    "TAC C/D (ng/mL per mg/day)" = tac_cd,
    "MPA trough (ug/mL)" = mpa,
    "MPAG trough (ug/mL)" = mpag,
    "AcMPAG trough (ug/mL)" = acmpag
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Typical-value troughs (CYP3A5 non-expresser, TAC 1 mg bid, MMF 500 mg bid,",
    "reference genotypes) after increasing lengths of dosing history."
  ))
stopifnot(all(diff(hist_tab$mpa) > 0), all(diff(hist_tab$tac_cd) > 0))
```

The paper's observed median troughs (Figure 1: MPA about 2 ug/mL, MPAG about
22 ug/mL, AcMPAG about 0.25 ug/mL, in patients on a median 500 mg MMF bid)
and its simulated C/D values sit near the 7-21-day rows, not near the
months-long accumulation that years of maintenance therapy would imply under
the printed parameters. The inclusion criterion required a dose that had been
stable for at least two weeks, so the vignette simulates a 14-day history.
This history is a simulation choice; the model parameters are as printed.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1 -- concentrations 0-4 h after the morning dose

Figure 1 of Kim 2019 shows prediction-corrected VPCs of the four analytes over
the 4-h sampling window. Without the observed data the panels below show the
simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles of the study-like cohort.

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 6}
fig1 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "Study cohort", tad <= 4) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = pmax(tad, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(tad, TAC = Cc, MPA = Cc_mpa, MPAG = Cc_mpag, AcMPAG = Cc_acmpag) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-tad, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = c("TAC", "MPA", "MPAG", "AcMPAG"))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = median(conc), Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig1, aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)",
       y = "Concentration (TAC: ng/mL; MPA, MPAG, AcMPAG: ug/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Kim 2019 (simulated median and 90% interval).") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-1-check}
fig1_med <- fig1 |>
  dplyr::filter(tad %in% c(0, 1, 2)) |>
  dplyr::select(analyte, tad, Q50) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tad, values_from = Q50, names_prefix = "t")
knitr::kable(dplyr::mutate(fig1_med, dplyr::across(-analyte, \(x) signif(x, 3))),
             caption = "Simulated medians at 0, 1 and 2 h after the dose.")
```

The observed medians read from Figure 1 are about 4, 9 and 9.5 ng/mL for TAC
(0, 1 and 2 h), 2, 9 and 4 ug/mL for MPA, 22, 38 and 44 ug/mL for MPAG and
0.25, 0.42 and 0.40 ug/mL for AcMPAG. The simulated MPA, MPAG and AcMPAG
medians agree with these readings to within about 25%. The simulated TAC
medians are about 30% lower (2.6, 6.7 and 6.9 ng/mL). The virtual cohort takes
1 mg TAC bid throughout, whereas the patients' doses ranged from 1 to 6 mg/day,
and Figure 1 is prediction-corrected, so its observed values are scaled to the
median population prediction rather than shown raw. The C/D comparison below
removes the dose question and agrees more closely.

```{r figure-1-gate}
tac_trough <- fig1_med$t0[fig1_med$analyte == "TAC"]
mpa_trough <- fig1_med$t0[fig1_med$analyte == "MPA"]
mpag_trough <- fig1_med$t0[fig1_med$analyte == "MPAG"]
stopifnot(
  # Within a factor of two of the Figure 1 observed median troughs. A unit
  # slip (ng vs ug, mg vs g) or a mis-transcribed clearance misses by far more.
  tac_trough > 2, tac_trough < 8,
  mpa_trough > 1, mpa_trough < 4,
  mpag_trough > 11, mpag_trough < 44
)
```

## Simulation -- trough per daily dose (C/D) by CYP3A5 and MMF dose

The paper reports the steady-state TAC trough per total daily dose (C/D,
ng/mL per mg) as mean +/- SD. Trough and the other exposure metrics of the last
dosing interval are computed with PKNCA, grouped by arm.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), arm != "Study cohort") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = pmax(tad, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm, tac_daily)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "hr")
dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, arm, tac_daily) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = tac_daily / 2)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Simulated TAC NCA over the last 12-h interval.")
```

```{r cd-compare}
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
cd <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_nca, id, tac_daily), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(cd = PPORRES / tac_daily) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_mean = mean(cd), sim_sd = stats::sd(cd), .groups = "drop")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                                     ~pub_mean, ~pub_sd,
  "CYP3A5 expresser, MMF 500 mg bid",            0.89,    0.44,
  "CYP3A5 expresser, MMF 1,000 mg bid",          1.24,    0.59,
  "CYP3A5 non-expresser, MMF 500 mg bid",        1.59,    0.67,
  "CYP3A5 non-expresser, MMF 1,000 mg bid",      2.14,    0.88
)
cd_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(published, cd, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_mean - pub_mean) / pub_mean)

cd_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(sim_mean, sim_sd, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, pub_mean, pub_sd, sim_mean, sim_sd, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Published mean C/D" = pub_mean,
    "Published SD" = pub_sd,
    "Simulated mean C/D" = sim_mean,
    "Simulated SD" = sim_sd,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "TAC trough per daily dose (ng/mL per mg/day): Kim 2019 Results",
    "(simulation of 1,000 per population) vs this simulation (200 per arm)."
  ))

mmf_effect <- cd_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(cyp = sub(",.*", "", arm), mmf = ifelse(grepl("1,000", arm), "hi", "lo")) |>
  dplyr::select(cyp, mmf, sim_mean, pub_mean) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mmf, values_from = c(sim_mean, pub_mean)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_increase = sim_mean_hi - sim_mean_lo,
                pub_increase = pub_mean_hi - pub_mean_lo)
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::select(mmf_effect, cyp, sim_increase, pub_increase) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-cyp, \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
    dplyr::rename("Genotype" = cyp, "Simulated increase in C/D" = sim_increase,
                  "Published increase in C/D" = pub_increase),
  caption = "Absolute increase in C/D from MMF 500 to 1,000 mg bid (abstract: 0.35 and 0.55)."
)

stopifnot(
  # Group means of 200 subjects: a centre measure, not an extreme.
  all(abs(cd_cmp$pct_diff) < 25),
  # Direction of both covariate effects (each about 30-40%).
  all(mmf_effect$sim_mean_hi > mmf_effect$sim_mean_lo),
  mmf_effect$sim_mean_lo[mmf_effect$cyp == "CYP3A5 non-expresser"] >
    mmf_effect$sim_mean_lo[mmf_effect$cyp == "CYP3A5 expresser"]
)
```

The simulated C/D values reproduce the published ordering (non-expressers
above expressers, MMF 1,000 mg above 500 mg). The simulated means run 4-10%
below the published means and the increase with the MMF dose is slightly
smaller (0.32 and 0.46 against 0.35 and 0.55); both are consistent with a
somewhat shorter dosing history than the authors used, which the paper does not
report. No parameter was adjusted to match them.

## SLCO1B3 and UGT2B7 have no visible effect on TAC

The paper reports that the two MMF-metabolite genotypes did not change TAC
C/D. In the model they act only on MPAG volume and AcMPAG formation; the
UGT2B7 effect lowers k59, which lowers total MPA metabolism by about 3% and so
raises MPA, and through Eq. 1 TAC, very slightly.

```{r genotype-check}
geno_cd <- function(slco, ugt) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 1, cmt = "depot", ii = 12, addl = 2 * n_days - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 500, cmt = "depot_mpa", ii = 12, addl = 2 * n_days - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(24 * n_days, cmt = "central")
  d <- as.data.frame(ev)
  d$dvid <- ifelse(d$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  d$CYP3A5_EXPR <- 0
  d$SNP_SLCO1B3_RS4149117_T_CARRIER <- slco
  d$SNP_UGT2B7_RS7439366_T_CARRIER <- ugt
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, d, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame",
                       useLinCmt = FALSE, maxsteps = 1e6)
  s$Cc[nrow(s)] / 2
}
geno <- expand.grid(slco = 0:1, ugt = 0:1)
geno$cd <- mapply(geno_cd, geno$slco, geno$ugt)
geno$pct_vs_ref <- 100 * (geno$cd / geno$cd[1] - 1)
knitr::kable(
  geno |>
    dplyr::mutate(cd = signif(cd, 3), pct_vs_ref = round(pct_vs_ref, 2)) |>
    dplyr::rename("SLCO1B3 T carrier" = slco, "UGT2B7 T carrier" = ugt,
                  "Typical C/D" = cd, "Change vs GG / CC (%)" = pct_vs_ref),
  caption = "Typical TAC C/D by metabolite genotype (non-expresser, MMF 500 mg bid)."
)
# The two metabolite genotypes are deterministic inputs to the same solve,
# so a tight bound is appropriate here.
stopifnot(all(abs(geno$pct_vs_ref) < 5), geno$pct_vs_ref[geno$slco == 1 & geno$ugt == 0] == 0)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dosing history of 14 days.** Under the printed parameters MPA accumulates
  in its peripheral compartment for months (k65 = 0.0089 1/h), while the
  paper's own observed troughs (Figure 1) and simulated C/D values match a
  history of roughly one to three weeks. The paper does not say how prior
  doses were entered in the NONMEM dataset or in the simulations it calls
  "steady state". The vignette uses 14 days, the stable-dose period required
  for inclusion. Users simulating long maintenance therapy should know that
  MPA, MPAG and the TAC interaction keep rising past this point under the
  model as published (see "How long a dosing history?").
- **Gallbladder emptying window per dose.** MTIME1 (7.96 h) and MTIME2 (1 h)
  are fixed values carried over from the single-dose healthy-volunteer model.
  For twice-daily dosing the window is anchored to the most recent MMF dose,
  so the gallbladder empties from 7.96 to 8.96 h after every dose. The paper
  does not describe how the meal time was handled for repeated dosing.
- **Derived rate constants.** `k57`, `k59` and `k78` are not tabulated. MPA
  leaves the central compartment only by metabolism (Figure 2), so
  `k57 + k59 = CL/F MPA / V/F MPA`, split by fMPA = 0.85, and EHC is the
  biliary share of MPAG elimination, `EHC = k78 / (k70 + k78)`. The same
  derivations are used in `Kim_2018_tacrolimus`.
- **UGT2B7 effect on k59 only.** Table 2 places the UGT2B7 effect on k59. It is
  applied to k59 after the fMPA split, so it also lowers total MPA metabolism
  slightly (by 15% x 18.8% = 2.8% in T carriers) rather than shifting the split
  at constant total clearance.
- **Residual-error values as standard deviations.** Table 2 lists the sigma
  values without saying whether they are variances or SDs. They are used as SDs
  (0.211 = 21.1% proportional error for TAC), the same reading as in
  `Kim_2018_tacrolimus`, and the additive TAC term (0.585) is in ng/mL.
- **Dosing in apparent units.** TAC and MMF doses are entered in mg of the
  administered drug; CL/F and V/F absorb bioavailability and the MMF to MPA
  conversion. TAC (whole blood) is reported in ng/mL, MPA, MPAG and AcMPAG
  (plasma) in ug/mL.
- **Typo in the Simulation section.** The paper's Results list "SLCO1B1
  genotype" among the simulated factors; the Methods and Table 2 make clear the
  covariate is SLCO1B3 rs4149117. The paper also writes the UGT2B7 SNP as
  802T>C in one place and 802C>T in others; both compare T carriers with CC.
- **Virtual cohort.** The paper simulated 1,000 subjects in each of 32
  populations; this vignette uses 200 per arm with TAC dose and the two
  metabolite genotypes drawn within each arm. The model has no continuous
  covariate, so weight and age are not simulated. Observed data are not
  public, so Figure 1 is shown as simulated percentiles only.
- **Errata.** No erratum or correction to Kim 2019 was found (Europe PMC
  correction links and erratum search checked 2026-11-25). The supplement contains only goodness-of-fit
  figures (Figures S1-S4) and no parameter values.
